The prerequisite is basic computer science knowledge (i.e. what is bits, bytes, programming and algorithm basics) Step 1: AI Basics 🔠 As a first step, we need to have a clear understanding of various concepts and disciplines in the world of AI at a higher level. We need to understand AI family tree along with the following concepts, • Topics o Machine Learning vs AI o Statistical vs Deep Learning o Supervised vs Unsupervised Learning o What is Gen AI, Agents, Agentic AI? o NLP and rule-based system

Murali krishna 23p61a67g9 23p61a67h5 24p65a6716 Title: Unified Multimodal RAG Evaluation Framework for Benchmarking Retrieval-Augmented Generation Systems. Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) has emerged as a powerful technique for enhancing the accuracy and reliability of Large Language Models by incorporating external knowledge sources. However, evaluating and comparing different RAG architectures, especially multimodal systems, remains a significant challenge due to the lack of standardized benchmarking methods. This project proposes a Unified Multimodal RAG Evaluation Framework that enables objective comparison of multiple RAG architectures using common datasets and evaluation metrics. The framework supports multimodal inputs such as text, images, tables, and PDFs, while measuring performance based on faithfulness, context precision, context recall, hallucination rate, semantic similarity, and response latency. It provides a real-time interactive interface that visualizes responses, retrieval quality, and performance metrics for each RAG system. By offering a unified benchmarking environment, the proposed framework helps researchers and developers analyze the strengths, limitations, and trade-offs of different Retrieval-Augmented Generation systems, promoting more reliable and reproducible RAG evaluation. ABSTRACT Accurate cropland classification is crucial for agricultural planning and food security. Traditional deep learning models often require large architectures to handle complex and imbalanced datasets. To address this, the proposed Cropland Quantum Learning system uses a hybrid quantum –classical neural network for cropland classification. Quantum variational circuits are employed for efficient feature learning, followed by a lightweight classical classifier. This approach reduces model complexity while maint aining competitive performance, and a web -based interface enables user input and real -time prediction with confidence scores. Keywords: Machine Learning, Satellite Imagery, Quantum Machine Learning, Crop detection. iv
